title.zh: 卷64 列傳第29 李圓通 陳茂 張定和 張奫 麥鐵杖 沈光 來護兒 魚俱羅 陳稜 王辯
title.en: Volume 64 Biographies 29: Li Yuantong, Chen Mao, Zhang Dinghe, Zhang Bian, Mai Tiezhang, Shen Guang, Lai Hua'er, Yu Juluo, Chen Leng, Wang Bian
title.raw: 卷64 列傳第29 李圓通 陳茂 張定和 張奫 麥鐵杖 沈光 來護兒 魚俱羅 陳稜 王辯 Volume 64 Biographies 29: Li Yuantong, Chen Mao, Zhang Dinghe, Zhang Bian, Mai Tiezhang, Shen Guang, Lai Hua'er, Yu Juluo, Chen Leng, Wang Bian

sentences.zh: 李圓通，京兆涇陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Yuantong—Li Yuantong was a native of Jingyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuantong was a native of Jingyang in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父景，以軍士隸武元皇帝，因與家僮黑女私，生圓通。

translations.literal: His father Jing, serving as a soldier under Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, had an illicit affair with a household slave named Hei Nü and fathered Yuantong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing served as a soldier under Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou. He had an affair with a household slave called Hei Nü, and she bore Yuantong.

sentences.zh: 景不之認，由是孤賤，給使高祖家。

translations.literal: Jing would not acknowledge him; because of this he was isolated and lowly, and was assigned as a servant in the household of the future Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Jing refused to acknowledge him, so Yuantong grew up isolated and in humble circumstances, working as a servant in the household of the future Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 及為隋國公，擢授參軍事。

translations.literal: When he became Duke of Sui, Yuantong was promoted and appointed military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Jian was made Duke of Sui, Yuantong was promoted to serve as his military adjutant.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖少時，每宴賓客，恆令圓通監廚。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the future Emperor Wen was young, whenever he entertained guests he always had Yuantong supervise the kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, whenever the future Emperor Wen held banquets for guests, he always put Yuantong in charge of the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 圓通性嚴整，左右婢僕咸所敬憚。

translations.literal: Yuantong was stern and orderly in character, and the maids and servants around him all respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong was stern and exacting by nature, and the maids and servants in the household all respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 唯世子乳母恃寵輕之，賓客未供，每有幹請，圓通不許，或輒持去。

translations.literal: Only the crown prince's wet nurse, relying on favor, treated him lightly; before the guests were served she would often make requests, which Yuantong would not allow, or she would simply take food away.
translations.idiomatic: Only the crown prince's wet nurse, secure in her favor, looked down on him. Before the guests had been served, she would often make demands; Yuantong refused them, or she would simply carry food away herself.

sentences.zh: 圓通大怒，叱廚人撾之數十，叫呼之聲徹於閤內，僚吏左右代其失色。

translations.literal: Yuantong was greatly angered and ordered the kitchen staff to beat her several dozen times; her cries resounded throughout the hall, and the officials and attendants nearby all turned pale on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong flew into a rage and had the kitchen staff beat her several dozen strokes. Her screams echoed through the hall, and the officials and attendants nearby all blanched in alarm.

sentences.zh: 賓去之後，高祖具知之，召圓通，命坐賜食，從此獨善之，以為堪當大任。

translations.literal: After the guests had left, the future Emperor Wen learned the full story, summoned Yuantong, ordered him to be seated and granted him food; from then on he favored him alone and considered him fit for great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: After the guests had gone, the future Emperor Wen learned what had happened. He summoned Yuantong, had him sit down, and shared a meal with him. From then on he favored Yuantong above others and judged him capable of great trust.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，賜封懷昌男。

translations.literal: When the future Emperor Wen became Chancellor, he granted Yuantong the title Baron of Huaichang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, he enfeoffed Yuantong as Baron of Huaichang.

sentences.zh: 久之，授帥都督，進爵新安子，委以心膂。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed commander-in-chief, advanced in rank to Viscount of Xin'an, and entrusted as a close confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed commander-in-chief, raised to Viscount of Xin'an, and entrusted as one of Yang Jian's closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 圓通多力勁捷，長於武用。

translations.literal: Yuantong was strong, vigorous, and nimble, and excelled in martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong was powerfully built, quick, and agile, and excelled in military matters.

sentences.zh: 周氏諸王素憚高祖，每伺高祖之隙，圖為不利，賴圓通保護，獲免者數矣。

translations.literal: The princes of the Zhou house had long feared the future Emperor Wen; they constantly watched for openings against him and plotted harm, but thanks to Yuantong's protection he escaped danger on numerous occasions.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of the Northern Zhou had long feared Yang Jian and constantly watched for chances to harm him. Time and again Yuantong's protection kept him from disaster.

sentences.zh: 高祖深感之，由是參預政事。

translations.literal: The future Emperor Wen was deeply grateful to him and from this time onward had him participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was deeply moved by his loyalty and from then on brought him into deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 授相國外兵曹，仍領左親信。

translations.literal: He was appointed to the Chancellor's bureau of external military affairs and also continued to command the left personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the Chancellor's bureau of external military affairs while continuing to command the left personal guard.

sentences.zh: 尋授上儀同。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜內史侍郎，領左衛長史，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When the future Emperor Wen received the abdication, Yuantong was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, concurrently served as Chief Clerk of the Left Guard, and was advanced in rank to Baron.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian accepted the throne, Yuantong was made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Chief Clerk of the Left Guard, and was raised to the rank of baron.

sentences.zh: 曆左右庶子、給事黃門侍郎、尚書左丞，攝刑部尚書，深被任信。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Left and Right Subordinate Tutor, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and acted as Minister of Justice; he was deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Left and Right Subordinate Tutor, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and acted as Minister of Justice, winning deep trust from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 後以左丞領左翊衛驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Later, while serving as Left Vice Director, he also commanded the Left Yiwu Guard as General of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while still Left Vice Director, he also commanded the Left Yiwu Guard with the title General of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，圓通以行軍總管從楊素出信州道，以功進位大將軍，進封萬安縣侯，拜揚州總管長史。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen, Yuantong served as campaign commander under Yang Su by way of the Xinzhou route; for his merit he was advanced to Grand General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wan'an County, and appointed Chief Clerk to the Governor-General of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen, Yuantong served as campaign commander under Yang Su on the Xinzhou route. For his achievements he was promoted to Grand General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wan'an, and appointed chief clerk to the Governor-General of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋轉并州總管長史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to serve as Chief Clerk to the Governor-General of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the same post under the Governor-General of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦孝王仁柔自善，少斷決，府中事多決於圓通。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Qin was benevolent, gentle, and self-contented, and seldom decisive; most affairs of his princely establishment were decided by Yuantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao of Qin was mild and easygoing and rarely decisive, so most matters in his household were settled by Yuantong.

sentences.zh: 入為司農卿、治粟內史，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Agriculture and Internal Secretary for Grain Administration, then was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Minister of Agriculture and Internal Secretary for Grain Administration, and later became Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，復為并州長史。

translations.literal: Several years later he again became Chief Clerk of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he returned to serve again as chief clerk of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝王以奢侈得罪，圓通亦坐免官。

translations.literal: The prince was punished for extravagance, and Yuantong was also dismissed from office on account of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was punished for extravagance, Yuantong was dismissed from office as well.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校刑部尚書事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed to inspect and oversee the affairs of the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，以勳舊進爵郡公。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era, as an old meritorious official he was advanced in rank to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he was raised to Duke of a commandery in recognition of his long service and merit.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Yuantong was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Yuantong was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 帝幸揚州，以圓通留守京師。

translations.literal: When the emperor traveled to Yangzhou, he left Yuantong behind to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went on tour to Yangzhou, he left Yuantong in charge of the capital.

sentences.zh: 判宇文述田以還民，述訴其受賂。

translations.literal: He adjudicated fields belonging to Yuwen Shu and returned them to the people; Shu accused him of having accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled that fields held by Yuwen Shu should be returned to the common people. Shu then accused him of taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 帝怒而徵之，見帝於洛陽，坐是免官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and summoned him; he met the emperor at Luoyang and on this account was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and summoned him to Luoyang, where he was stripped of office on that charge.

sentences.zh: 圓通憂懼發疾而卒。

translations.literal: Yuantong, anxious and fearful, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with anxiety and fear, Yuantong fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 贈柱國，封爵悉如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the title Pillar of State, and all his enfeoffments remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Pillar of State, and all his titles were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 子孝常，大業末，為華陰令。

translations.literal: His son Xiaochang, at the end of the Daye era, served as magistrate of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaochang served as magistrate of Huayin late in the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 陳茂，河東猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Chen Mao—Chen Mao was a native of Yishi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mao was a native of Yishi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 家世寒微，質直恭謹，為州裡所敬。

translations.literal: His family had long been humble; he was honest, upright, respectful, and cautious, and was esteemed in his district.
translations.idiomatic: His family was of humble origin. Plainspoken, upright, and respectful, he was held in esteem throughout his district.

sentences.zh: 高祖為隋國公，引為僚佐，遇待與圓通等。

translations.literal: When the future Emperor Wen became Duke of Sui, he brought Mao in as a staff member and treated him with the same favor as Yuantong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was made Duke of Sui, he took Mao onto his staff and treated him with the same regard as Yuantong.

sentences.zh: 每令典家事，未嘗不稱旨，高祖善之。

translations.literal: Whenever he was put in charge of household affairs he never failed to meet expectations, and the future Emperor Wen was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was put in charge of household affairs he never failed to please, and Yang Jian came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 後從高祖與齊師戰于晉州，賊甚盛，高祖將挑戰，茂固止不得，因捉馬鞚。

translations.literal: Later he followed the future Emperor Wen in battle against the Qi army at Jinzhou; the enemy was very strong and the future Emperor Wen was about to offer battle, but Mao firmly restrained him and would not allow it, seizing the horse's reins.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yang Jian fought the Qi army at Jinzhou, the enemy force was overwhelming and Yang Jian was about to engage. Mao held him back by force, gripping the horse's reins.

sentences.zh: 高祖忿之，拔刀斫其額，流血被面，詞氣不撓。

translations.literal: The future Emperor Wen was angry, drew his sword, and struck Mao's forehead; blood covered his face, yet his tone did not falter.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian flew into a rage, drew his sword, and struck Mao across the forehead until blood covered his face, yet Mao's manner did not waver.

sentences.zh: 高祖感而謝之，厚加禮敬。

translations.literal: The future Emperor Wen was moved and apologized to him, treating him with great courtesy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his loyalty, Yang Jian apologized and treated him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 其後官至上士。

translations.literal: Thereafter he rose in office to Senior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to the rank of Senior Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，委以心膂。

translations.literal: When the future Emperor Wen became Chancellor, he entrusted Mao as a close confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, he entrusted Mao as one of his closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜給事黃門侍郎，封魏城縣男，每典機密。

translations.literal: When the abdication was accepted, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed as Baron of Weicheng County, and regularly handled confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Mao was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed as Baron of Weicheng, and regularly handled confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 在官十餘年，轉益州總管司馬，遷太府卿，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: After more than ten years in office he was transferred to Military Aide to the Governor-General of Yizhou, then promoted to Minister of the Palace Storehouses and advanced in rank to Baron.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years in office he became military aide to the Governor-General of Yizhou, then Minister of the Palace Storehouses, and was raised to baron.

sentences.zh: 後數載，卒官。

translations.literal: Several years later he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 子政嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 政字弘道，倜儻有文武大略，善鐘律，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Zheng, style name Hongdao, was free-spirited and possessed broad talent in both civil and military affairs; he was skilled in pitch pipes and scales and adept with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, whose style was Hongdao, was bold and unconventional, with broad talent in both civil and military affairs. He was skilled in music theory and expert in archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 少養宮中，年十七，為太子千牛備身。

translations.literal: He was raised in the palace from youth; at seventeen he became an armed attendant of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in the palace from childhood, he became an armed attendant to the crown prince at seventeen.

sentences.zh: 時京師大俠劉居士重政才氣，數從之遊。

translations.literal: At that time the great knight-errant of the capital Liu Jushi valued Zheng's talent and spirit and often associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Jushi, a celebrated man of the capital's underworld, admired Zheng's talent and often kept his company.

sentences.zh: 圓通子孝常與政相善，並與居士交結。

translations.literal: Yuantong's son Xiaochang was on good terms with Zheng, and both were connected with Jushi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong's son Xiaochang was close to Zheng, and both were tied to Jushi's circle.

sentences.zh: 及居士下獄誅，政及孝常當從坐，上以功臣子，撻之二百而赦之。

translations.literal: When Jushi was imprisoned and executed, Zheng and Xiaochang were liable to punishment by association; because they were sons of meritorious officials, the emperor had them flogged two hundred strokes and then pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jushi was imprisoned and executed, Zheng and Xiaochang were due to be punished as associates. Because they were sons of meritorious officials, the emperor had them flogged two hundred strokes and then pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 由是不得調。

translations.literal: Because of this he was not given regular appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After that he was passed over for regular appointments.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，授協律郎，遷通事謁者，兵曹承務郎。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yang's reign he was appointed Harmonizer, then transferred to Protocol Officer and Assistant in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he was appointed Harmonizer, then Protocol Officer and assistant in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝美其才，甚重之。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his talent and valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his talent and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之亂也，以為太常卿。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Yuwen Huaji he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuwen Huaji's rebellion he was made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 後歸大唐，卒于梁州總管。

translations.literal: Later he submitted to the Great Tang and died while serving as Governor-General of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted to the Tang and died while serving as Governor-General of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 張定和，字處謐，京兆萬年人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Dinghe—Zhang Dinghe, style name Chumi, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dinghe, whose style was Chumi, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少貧賤，有志節。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and lowly but possessed resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up poor but was known for his resolve and integrity.

sentences.zh: 初為侍官。

translations.literal: At first he served as an attendant officer.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as an attendant officer.

sentences.zh: 會平陳之役，定和當從征，無以自給。

translations.literal: When the campaign to pacify Chen arose, Dinghe was to join the expedition but had no means to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign to conquer Chen began, Dinghe was called to join the army but had no money for the journey.

sentences.zh: 其妻有嫁時衣服，定和將鬻之，妻靳固不與，定和於是遂行。

translations.literal: His wife had the clothes from her wedding; Dinghe was about to sell them, but his wife firmly refused to give them up, and Dinghe set out anyway.
translations.idiomatic: His wife still had her wedding clothes. Dinghe meant to sell them, but she refused to part with them, so he set out for the campaign all the same.

sentences.zh: 以功拜儀同，賜帛千匹，遂棄其妻。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Pillar of State, granted a thousand bolts of silk, and then abandoned his wife.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made Pillar of State and given a thousand bolts of silk, after which he cast off his wife.

sentences.zh: 是後數以軍功加上開府、驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Thereafter, on repeated military achievements, he was advanced to Superlative Pillar of State and General of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After that he rose repeatedly through military merit to Superlative Pillar of State and General of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從上柱國李充擊突厥，先登陷陣，虜刺之中頸，定和以草塞創而戰，神氣自若，虜遂敗走。

translations.literal: Following the Supreme Pillar Li Chong against the Turks, he was first to ascend and break the enemy line; the barbarians pierced him in the neck, but Dinghe stuffed the wound with grass and continued fighting, his bearing calm as before, and the enemy fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under the Supreme Pillar Li Chong against the Turks, he was first over the ramparts into the enemy line. A Turk spear struck him in the neck; he stuffed the wound with grass and kept fighting, calm as ever, until the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 上聞而壯之，遣使者齎藥，馳詣定和所勞問之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he admired his valor and sent an envoy bearing medicine, riding in haste to Dinghe's position to console and inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed by his courage and sent an envoy with medicine, riding posthaste to Dinghe's camp to commend him.

sentences.zh: 進位柱國，封武安縣侯，賞物二千段，良馬二匹，金百兩。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an County, and rewarded with two thousand lengths of goods, two fine horses, and a hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an, with rewards of two thousand lengths of goods, two fine horses, and a hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜宜州刺史，尋轉河內太守，頗有惠政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Dinghe was appointed Governor of Yizhou, then transferred to Administrator of Henei, where he showed considerable benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Dinghe was made Governor of Yizhou and soon transferred to Administrator of Henei, where he earned a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，徵拜左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he was recalled and appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 從帝征吐谷渾，至覆袁川。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the campaign against the Tuyuhun as far as Fuyuan River.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the campaign against the Tuyuhun as far as Fuyuan River.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾主與數騎而遁，其名王詐為渾主，保車我真山，帝命定和率師擊之。

translations.literal: At that time the Tuyuhun ruler fled with only a few horsemen; a noble falsely posed as the ruler and held Chewozhen Mountain, and the emperor ordered Dinghe to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun ruler had fled with only a handful of horsemen. A noble pretended to be the ruler and held Chewozhen Mountain, and the emperor ordered Dinghe to attack him.

sentences.zh: 既與賊相遇，輕其眾少，呼之令降，賊不肯下。

translations.literal: Once he met the enemy he despised their small numbers, called on them to surrender, but the enemy would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: When he met the enemy he scorned their small numbers and called on them to surrender, but they refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 定和不被甲，挺身登山，賊伏兵于岩穀之下，發矢中之而斃。

translations.literal: Dinghe did not don armor, but advanced up the mountain in person; the enemy had hidden troops below the cliffs and ravines, loosed arrows, struck him, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Dinghe went up the mountain without armor. Enemy troops lay in ambush in the ravines below and shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 其亞將柳武建擊賊，悉斬之。

translations.literal: His second-in-command Liu Wujian attacked the enemy and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: His second-in-command Liu Wujian attacked the enemy and cut them down to the last man.

sentences.zh: 帝為流涕，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him and posthumously awarded him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept over his death and posthumously honored him as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時舊爵例除，於是復封武安侯，諡曰壯武。

translations.literal: At that time old enfeoffments were routinely abolished by regulation, so he was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an, with the posthumous title Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Because old titles were usually abolished by regulation at the time, he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an with the posthumous name Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 贈絹千匹，米千石。

translations.literal: There were granted posthumously a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand bolts of silk and a thousand piculs of grain were granted to his family.

sentences.zh: 子世立嗣，尋拜為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Shili succeeded him and was soon appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shili succeeded him and was soon made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 張奫，字文懿，自雲清河人也，家于淮陰。

translations.literal: Zhang Ben—Zhang Ben, style name Wenyi, claimed descent from Qinghe and made his home in Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ben, whose style was Wenyi, claimed descent from Qinghe and lived in Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 好讀兵書，尤便刀楯。

translations.literal: He loved reading military texts and was especially skilled with sword and shield.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading military texts and was especially adept with sword and shield.

sentences.zh: 周世，鄉人郭子翼密引陳寇，奫父雙欲率子弟擊之，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: During the Zhou period a fellow townsman named Guo Ziyi secretly brought in Chen raiders; Ben's father Shuang wished to lead the clan youths to attack them but hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Northern Zhou, a townsman named Guo Ziyi secretly guided Chen raiders into the area. Ben's father Shuang wanted to lead the clan's young men against them but could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 奫贊成其謀，竟以破賊，由是以勇決知名。

translations.literal: Ben supported the plan, and in the end they defeated the bandits; from this he became known for courage and decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Ben urged the plan through, and they routed the raiders. From that time he was known for courage and resolve.

sentences.zh: 起家州主簿。

translations.literal: He began his career as a prefectural registrar.
translations.idiomatic: He began his official career as a prefectural registrar.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，授大都督，領鄉兵。

translations.literal: When the future Emperor Wen became Chancellor, he appointed Ben Grand Commander and put him in charge of local militia.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, he appointed Ben Grand Commander and put him in charge of local militia.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼之鎮壽春也，恆為間諜，平陳之役，頗有功焉。

translations.literal: When He Ruo Bi was stationed at Shouchun, Ben constantly served as a spy; in the campaign to pacify Chen he rendered considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: While He Ruobi held Shouchun, Ben regularly served as his spy. In the conquest of Chen he distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 進位開府儀同三司，封文安縣子，邑八百戶，賜物二千五百段，粟二千五百石。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Defender-in-Chief with the privileges of the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an County with an estate of eight hundred households, and granted two thousand five hundred lengths of goods and two thousand five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Defender-in-Chief with the privileges of the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an with eight hundred households, and given two thousand five hundred lengths of goods and two thousand five hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，率水軍破逆賊笮子游於京口、薛子建於和州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he led the naval forces to defeat the rebel Ze Ziyou at Jingkou and Xue Zijian at Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he led the fleet to defeat the rebels Ze Ziyou at Jingkou and Xue Zijian at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 徵入朝，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned to court and appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 高祖命升御坐而宴之，謂奫曰：「卿可為朕兒，朕為卿父。

translations.literal: The future Emperor Wen ordered him to ascend the imperial seat and be feasted, saying to Ben: "You may be my son, and I shall be your father.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him take a place on the imperial dais and feast with him, saying, "You may be my son, and I your father.

sentences.zh: 今日聚集，示無外也。」

translations.literal: Today's gathering shows that there is no outsider between us.
translations.idiomatic: Today's gathering shows there is no distance between us.

sentences.zh: 其後賜綺羅千匹，綠沉甲、獸文具裝。

translations.literal: Afterward he was granted a thousand bolts of fine silk, a Lüchen armor set, and a full suit of beast-patterned military gear.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he received a thousand bolts of fine silk, a suit of Lüchen armor, and a full set of beast-patterned military equipment.

sentences.zh: 尋從楊素征江表，別破高智慧於會稽、吳世華於臨海。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he followed Yang Su in the campaign south of the Yangzi, separately defeating Gao Zhihui at Kuaiji and Wu Shihua at Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Yang Su south of the Yangzi, separately defeating Gao Zhihui at Kuaiji and Wu Shihua at Linhai.

sentences.zh: 進位上大將軍，賜奴婢六十口，縑彩三百匹。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Senior Grand General and granted sixty household slaves and three hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Grand General and given sixty household slaves and three hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 曆撫、顯、齊三州刺史，俱有能名，

translations.literal: He successively served as Governor of Fu, Xian, and Qi prefectures, all with a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Fu, Xian, and Qi, earning a reputation for competence in each post.

sentences.zh: 開皇十八年，為行軍總管，從漢王諒征遼東。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, he served as campaign commander and followed Prince of Han Liang on the expedition against Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, he served as campaign commander and followed Prince Liang of Han on the expedition against Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 諸軍多物故，奫眾獨全。

translations.literal: Many of the armies suffered heavy losses, but Ben's forces alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the armies suffered heavy losses, but Ben's troops alone came through intact.

sentences.zh: 高祖善之，賜物二百五十段。

translations.literal: The future Emperor Wen was pleased with him and granted him two hundred fifty lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and rewarded him with two hundred fifty lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，遷潭州總管，在職三年卒。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era he was transferred to Governor-General of Tanzhou and died in office after three years.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he was made Governor-General of Tanzhou and died in office after three years.

sentences.zh: 有子孝廉。

translations.literal: He had a son named Xiaolian.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Xiaolian.

sentences.zh: 麥鐵杖，始興人也。

translations.literal: Mai Tiezhang—Mai Tiezhang was a native of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Mai Tiezhang was a native of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 驍勇有膂力，日行五百里，走及奔馬。

translations.literal: He was fierce and brave, with great physical strength; he could travel five hundred li in a day and run as fast as a galloping horse.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and powerfully built, he could cover five hundred li in a day and keep pace with a galloping horse.

sentences.zh: 性疏誕使酒，好交遊，重信義，每以漁獵為事，不治產業。

translations.literal: By nature he was unrestrained, eccentric, and fond of drink; he loved making friends, valued faith and righteousness, and constantly took fishing and hunting as his occupation, not managing any estate.
translations.idiomatic: Unrestrained and eccentric, he drank heavily, loved company, and prized loyalty. He spent his days fishing and hunting and never troubled himself with property or business.

sentences.zh: 陳太建中，結聚為群盜，廣州刺史歐陽頠俘之以獻，沒為官戶，配執禦傘。

translations.literal: During the Taikang era of Chen he gathered a band of robbers; the Governor of Guangzhou Ouyang He captured him and presented him as tribute; he was made a government household slave and assigned to hold the imperial parasol.
translations.idiomatic: During Chen's Taikang era he led a band of robbers until Ouyang He, governor of Guangzhou, captured him and sent him up as tribute. He was made a government slave and assigned to hold the imperial parasol at court.

sentences.zh: 每罷朝後，行百餘里，夜至南徐州，俞城而入，行光火劫盜。

translations.literal: After each dismissal of court he would travel more than a hundred li, reach Southern Xuzhou by night, climb the city wall to enter, and carry out torch-lit robbery.
translations.idiomatic: After court each day he would travel more than a hundred li, reach Southern Xuzhou by night, scale the walls, and rob by torchlight.

sentences.zh: 旦還，及時仍又執傘。

translations.literal: At dawn he would return and, right on time, again hold the parasol.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn he was back, and at the proper hour he was again holding the parasol at court.

sentences.zh: 如此者十餘度，物主識之，州以狀奏。

translations.literal: This happened more than ten times; the owners of the goods recognized him, and the prefecture reported the matter in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: This happened more than ten times until victims recognized him and the prefecture reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朝士見鐵杖每旦恆在，不之信也。

translations.literal: Court officials saw Tiezhang at his post every morning and did not believe the report.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials saw Tiezhang at his post every morning and refused to believe it.

sentences.zh: 後數告變，尚書蔡徵曰：「此可驗耳。」

translations.literal: After repeated reports of irregularities, Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Cai Zheng said: "This can be tested."
translations.idiomatic: After repeated reports, Minister Cai Zheng said, "This can be tested."

sentences.zh: 于仗下時，購以百金，求人送詔書與南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When the court was dismissed below the halberds, he offered a hundred in gold to anyone who would deliver an imperial edict to the Governor of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When court was dismissed, he offered a hundred in gold for someone to deliver an imperial edict to the governor of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 鐵杖出應募，齎敕而往，明旦及奏事。

translations.literal: Tiezhang came forward to answer the call, carried the edict and went; by the next dawn he had returned and reported on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhang volunteered, carried the edict south, and was back by the next dawn to report.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「信然，為盜明矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is true—his thievery is now clear."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So it is true. His thievery is proven."

sentences.zh: 惜其勇捷，誡而釋之。

translations.literal: Yet he prized his courage and agility, admonished him, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor valued his courage, admonished him, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 陳亡後，徙居清流縣。

translations.literal: After the fall of Chen he moved to Qingliu County.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he moved to Qingliu County.

sentences.zh: 遇江東反，楊素遣鐵杖頭戴草束，夜浮渡江，覘賊中消息，具知還報。

translations.literal: When rebellion broke out east of the Yangzi, Yang Su sent Tiezhang with a bundle of grass on his head to float across the river by night, spy on news within the rebel camp, learn everything, and return to report.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in the lower Yangzi region, Yang Su sent Tiezhang with a bundle of grass on his head to swim the river by night, spy on the rebels, and return with a full report.

sentences.zh: 後復更往，為賊所擒。

translations.literal: Later he went again and was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He went again later and was captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 逆帥李棱遣兵仗三十人衛之，縛送高智慧。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Li Leng sent thirty armed men to guard him and bound him for delivery to Gao Zhihui.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Li Leng sent thirty armed men to escort him, bound, to Gao Zhihui.

sentences.zh: 行至慶亭，衛者憩食，哀其餒，解手以給其餐。

translations.literal: When they reached Qingting the guards rested to eat; pitying his hunger, they untied his hands to give him food.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingting the guards stopped to eat. Pitying his hunger, they untied his hands so he could eat.

sentences.zh: 鐵杖取賊刀，亂斬衛者，殺之皆盡，悉割其鼻，懷之以歸。

translations.literal: Tiezhang seized a rebel sword, hacked wildly at the guards, killed them all, cut off all their noses, and carried them back with him.
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhang seized a sword, cut down every guard, sliced off all their noses, and carried them back as proof.

sentences.zh: 素大奇之。

translations.literal: Yang Su was greatly astonished by him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su was astonished.

sentences.zh: 後敘戰勳，不及鐵杖，遇素馳驛歸於京師，鐵杖步追之，每夜則同宿。

translations.literal: Later when battle merits were recorded, Tiezhang was left out; encountering Yang Su galloping posthorses back to the capital, Tiezhang pursued on foot and each night they lodged together.
translations.idiomatic: When battle honors were recorded, Tiezhang was left out. Yang Su rode posthorses back to the capital; Tiezhang ran after him on foot and lodged with him each night.

sentences.zh: 素見而悟，特奏授儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Yang Su saw this he understood, and specially memorialized to appoint him Defender-in-Chief with the privileges of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su understood and specially recommended him for Defender-in-Chief with the privileges of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 以不識書，放還鄉里。

translations.literal: Because he could not read, he was sent back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was illiterate, he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 成陽公李徹稱其驍武，，徵至京師，除車騎將軍，仍從楊素北征突厥，加上開府。

translations.literal: Duke of Chengyang Li Che praised his fierce martial prowess; he was summoned to the capital, appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry, followed Yang Su on the northern campaign against the Turks, and was advanced to Superlative Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Li Che, Duke of Chengyang, praised his fighting skill. Summoned to the capital, he was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry, joined Yang Su against the Turks, and rose to Superlative Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，漢王諒反於并州，又從楊素擊之，每戰先登。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Prince of Han Liang rebelled at Bingzhou; Tiezhang again followed Yang Su to attack him and in every battle was first to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Prince Liang of Han rebelled at Bingzhou. Tiezhang again followed Yang Su and was first over the ramparts in every battle.

sentences.zh: 進位柱國。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 尋除萊州刺史，無治名。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Governor of Laizhou but earned no reputation for governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Laizhou but left no mark as an administrator.

sentences.zh: 後轉汝南太守，稍習法令，群盜屏跡。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Administrator of Runan, gradually learned statutes and ordinances, and bandits vanished from his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Runan as administrator, he gradually mastered the law and drove bandits from the region.

sentences.zh: 後因朝集，考功郎竇威嘲之曰：「麥是何姓？」

translations.literal: Later, during an assembly at court, Reviewing Officer Dou Wei mocked him, saying: "What sort of surname is Mai?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a court assembly, Reviewing Officer Dou Wei mocked him: "What kind of surname is Mai?"

sentences.zh: 鐵杖應口對曰：「麥豆不殊，那忽相怪！」

translations.literal: Tiezhang answered on the spot: "Mai and beans are not so different—why be surprised at all!"
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhang shot back, "Wheat and beans are much the same—why make such a fuss?"

sentences.zh: 威赧然，無以應之，時人以為敏慧。

translations.literal: Wei flushed with embarrassment and had no reply; people of the time considered this quick-witted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei flushed and had nothing to say; contemporaries judged him quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 尋除右屯衛大將軍，帝待之逾密。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand General of the Right Tunwei Guard, and the emperor treated him with ever greater intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand General of the Right Tunwei Guard, and the emperor drew him ever closer.

sentences.zh: 鐵杖自以荷恩深重，每懷竭命之志。

translations.literal: Tiezhang, considering himself deeply indebted for imperial favor, constantly harbored the resolve to give his life.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply conscious of the emperor's favor, he was always ready to give his life.

sentences.zh: 及遼東之役，請為前鋒，顧謂醫者吳景賢曰：「大丈夫性命自有所在，豈能艾炷灸頞，瓜蒂噴鼻，治黃不差，而臥死兒女手中乎？」

translations.literal: When the Liaodong campaign came, he asked to serve as vanguard and, turning to the physician Wu Jingxian, said: "A great man's life has its own place—how could he endure moxibustion on the forehead, melon-stem powder up the nose, treatment for jaundice that does not cure, and die in bed in the hands of wife and children?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Liaodong campaign began, he volunteered for the vanguard and told the physician Wu Jingxian, "A real man's life belongs on the battlefield. Am I to endure moxibustion on my brow and melon-stem up my nose for jaundice, then die in bed like a child?"

sentences.zh: 將渡遼，謂其三子曰：「阿奴當備淺色黃衫。

translations.literal: About to cross the Liao, he told his three sons: "You boys should prepare light-colored yellow coats.
translations.idiomatic: Before crossing the Liao, he told his three sons, "You should keep light yellow coats ready.

sentences.zh: 吾荷國恩，今是死日。

translations.literal: I owe the state a great debt; today is the day I die.
translations.idiomatic: I owe the state everything. Today I die.

sentences.zh: 我既被殺，爾當富貴。

translations.literal: Once I am killed, you will become rich and honored.
translations.idiomatic: When I am killed, you will rise to wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 唯誠與孝，爾其勉之。」

translations.literal: Only sincerity and filial piety—strive in these."
translations.idiomatic: Hold fast to sincerity and filial piety."

sentences.zh: 及濟，橋未成，去東岸尚數丈，賊大至。

translations.literal: When they crossed, the bridge was not yet finished and they were still several zhang from the eastern bank when the enemy came in force.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed before the bridge was finished, still several zhang from the eastern bank, when the enemy swarmed in.

sentences.zh: 鐵杖跳上岸，與賊戰，死。

translations.literal: Tiezhang leaped ashore, fought the enemy, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhang leaped ashore, fought the enemy, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 武賁郎將錢士雄、孟金叉亦死之，左右更無及者。

translations.literal: Martial Guardsmen Qian Shixiong and Meng Jincha also died; none of those around could keep up with them.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Guardsmen Qian Shixiong and Meng Jincha died with him; none of those nearby could match their valor.

sentences.zh: 帝為之流涕，購得其屍，下詔曰：「鐵杖志氣驍果，夙著勳庸，陪麾問罪，先登陷陣，節高義烈，身殞功存。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him, purchased his corpse, and issued an edict saying: "Tiezhang's spirit was fierce and resolute; long renowned for merit, he followed the banners to punish guilt, was first to ascend and break the enemy line; his integrity was lofty and his righteousness ardent—though his body perished, his achievement endures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept, bought back his body, and issued an edict: "Tiezhang was fierce in spirit and long famed for merit. He followed the banners to punish the enemy and was first into the breach. Though he fell, his achievement endures.

sentences.zh: 興言至誠，追懷傷悼，宜賚殊榮。

translations.literal: Speaking with utmost sincerity, in retrospective grief and mourning, he should be granted extraordinary honor.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to deepest grief, We grant him extraordinary honors.

sentences.zh: 用彰飾德。

translations.literal: Thus to display and adorn virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Let this display Our regard for loyal virtue.

sentences.zh: 可贈光祿大夫、宿國公。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Duke of Suguo.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Duke of Suguo.

sentences.zh: 諡曰武烈。」

translations.literal: His posthumous title is Wulie."
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name is Wulie."

sentences.zh: 子孟才嗣。

translations.literal: His son Mengcai succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mengcai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 尋授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 孟才有二弟，仲才、季才，俱拜正議大夫。

translations.literal: Mengcai had two younger brothers, Zhongcai and Jicai, all appointed Rectifier Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai had two younger brothers, Zhongcai and Jicai, who were also made Rectifier Grandees.

sentences.zh: 賵贈巨萬，賜轀輬車，給前後部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts amounted to tens of thousands; he was granted a funeral carriage and given front and rear escorts with feathered banners and martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts ran to tens of thousands. He received a funeral carriage and front and rear escorts with feathered banners and martial music.

sentences.zh: 平壤道敗將宇文述等百餘人皆為執紼，王公已下送至郊外，士雄贈左光祿大夫、右屯衛將軍、武強侯，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: More than a hundred defeated generals of the Pingrang route, including Yuwen Shu, all served as pallbearers; princes and dukes down to commoners escorted him to the suburbs. Shixiong was posthumously awarded Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, General of the Right Tunwei Guard, and Marquis of Wuqiang, with the posthumous title Gang.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred defeated commanders of the Pingrang campaign, including Yuwen Shu, served as pallbearers, and nobles escorted the procession to the suburbs. Shixiong was posthumously honored as Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, General of the Right Tunwei Guard, and Marquis of Wuqiang, with the posthumous name Gang.

sentences.zh: 子傑嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jie succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 金叉贈右光祿大夫，子善誼襲官。

translations.literal: Jincha was posthumously awarded Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; his son Shanyi inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: Jincha was posthumously honored as Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; his son Shanyi inherited his post.

sentences.zh: 孟才字智棱，果烈有父風。

translations.literal: Mengcai, style name Zhileng, was resolute and fierce in his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai, whose style was Zhileng, was bold and fierce like his father.

sentences.zh: 帝以孟才死節將子，恩賜殊厚，拜武賁郎將。

translations.literal: Because Mengcai was the son of a general who died for integrity, the emperor favored him with exceptional grace and appointed him Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a general who died for the throne, Mengcai received exceptional favor and was made Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 及江都之難，慨然有復仇之志。

translations.literal: When the disaster at Jiangdu occurred, he was stirred with the resolve to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck at Jiangdu, he burned with the desire for revenge.

sentences.zh: 與武牙郎錢傑素交友，二人相謂曰：「吾等世荷國恩，門著誠節。

translations.literal: He had long been friends with Martial Guard Qian Jie; the two said to each other: "Our families for generations have owed the state a debt of grace, and our houses are renowned for loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Martial Guard Qian Jie. Together they said, "Our families have owed the state for generations, and our houses are known for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今賊臣弑逆，社稷淪亡，無節可紀，何面目視息世間哉！」

translations.literal: Now a traitorous minister has murdered his sovereign and the altars of state are ruined—there is no integrity left to record; with what face can we go on living in this world!"
translations.idiomatic: Now a traitor has murdered the emperor and the realm is lost. What integrity is left to us? How can we go on living?"

sentences.zh: 於是流涕扼腕，遂相與謀，糾合恩舊，欲于顯福宮邀擊宇文化及。

translations.literal: Thereupon, weeping and wringing their wrists, they plotted together, gathered old friends bound by grace, and intended to ambush Yuwen Huaji at Xianfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, they swore to gather loyal friends and ambush Yuwen Huaji at Xianfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 事臨發，陳籓之子謙知其謀而告之，與其党沈光俱為化及所害，忠義之士哀焉。

translations.literal: When the affair was about to be launched, Chen Fan's son Qian learned of the plot and reported it; together with his comrade Shen Guang he was killed by Huaji, and men of loyalty and righteousness mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: Just before the attack, Chen Fan's son Qian betrayed the plot. Mengcai and his comrade Shen Guang were killed by Huaji, and loyal men mourned them.

sentences.zh: 沈光，字總持，吳興人也。

translations.literal: Shen Guang—Shen Guang, style name Zongchi, was a native of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Guang, whose style was Zongchi, was a native of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父君道，仕陳吏部侍郎，陳滅，家于長安。

translations.literal: His father Jundao served Chen as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; when Chen fell, the family settled in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jundao had been Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel under Chen; after Chen fell, the family settled in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇引署學士。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong brought him in and appointed him a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong took him on as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 後為漢王諒府掾，諒敗，除名。

translations.literal: Later he served as an aide in the establishment of Prince of Han Liang; when Liang was defeated, his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Prince Liang of Han; when the prince was defeated, Guang was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 光少驍捷，善戲馬，為天下之最。

translations.literal: Guang in youth was fierce and nimble, skilled in horsemanship and acrobatic riding, the best in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was swift and daring, unmatched in horsemanship and acrobatic riding.

sentences.zh: 略綜書記，微有詞藻，常慕立功名，不拘小節。

translations.literal: He had some command of written records and slight literary polish, constantly aspired to establish merit and fame, and did not fuss over small proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: He had some learning and a touch of literary skill, longed to win fame, and cared little for convention.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧窶，父兄並以傭書為事，光獨跅馳，交通輕俠，為京師惡少年之所朋附。

translations.literal: The family was very poor; father and brothers all made their living by copying books for hire, while Guang alone roamed freely, consorted with light-minded knights-errant, and was joined by the capital's unruly youths.
translations.idiomatic: The family was desperately poor; his father and brothers copied books for hire while Guang roamed the capital with ruffians and knights-errant.

sentences.zh: 人多贍遺，得以養親，每致甘食美服，未嘗困匱。

translations.literal: Many people gave him gifts, so he could support his parents; he always provided fine food and beautiful clothes and never knew want.
translations.idiomatic: Many gave him gifts, so he could support his parents with fine food and clothing and never knew want.

sentences.zh: 初建禪定寺，其中幡竿高十餘丈，適遇繩絕，非人力所及，諸僧患之。

translations.literal: When Chanding Temple was first built, its banner pole stood more than ten zhang high; the rope happened to break and was beyond human reach, to the distress of the monks.
translations.idiomatic: When Chanding Temple was built, its banner pole stood more than ten zhang high. The rope broke beyond anyone's reach, and the monks were at a loss.

sentences.zh: 光見而謂僧曰：「可持繩來，當相為上耳。」

translations.literal: Guang saw this and said to the monks: "Bring the rope—I will go up for you."
translations.idiomatic: Guang told the monks, "Bring the rope. I will go up for you."

sentences.zh: 諸僧驚喜，因取而與之。

translations.literal: The monks were startled and delighted and therefore took it and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: The monks were astonished and gladly handed it over.

sentences.zh: 光以口銜索，拍竿而上，直至龍頭。

translations.literal: Guang held the rope in his mouth, slapped the pole and climbed up, reaching all the way to the dragon head.
translations.idiomatic: He took the rope in his teeth, climbed hand over hand to the dragon head, and tied it off.

sentences.zh: 繫繩畢，手足皆放，透空而下，以掌拒地，倒行數十步。

translations.literal: When the rope was secured he let go with hands and feet, dropped through the air, caught the ground with his palms, and walked backward several dozen steps.
translations.idiomatic: When the rope was secured he let go, dropped through the air, caught himself on his palms, and walked backward several dozen steps.

sentences.zh: 觀者駭悅，莫不嗟異，時人號為「肉飛仙」。

translations.literal: Spectators were awed and delighted; none failed to marvel, and people of the time called him the "Flesh-Flying Immortal."
translations.idiomatic: Spectators were awestruck, and contemporaries called him the "Flesh-Flying Immortal."

sentences.zh: 大業中，煬帝徵天下驍果之士以伐遼左，光預焉。

translations.literal: During the Daye era Emperor Yang recruited fierce warriors from throughout the realm to campaign in eastern Liaodong; Guang was among them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era Emperor Yang recruited fierce warriors from across the realm for the Liaodong campaign; Guang was among them.

sentences.zh: 同類數萬人，皆出其下。

translations.literal: Among tens of thousands of his kind, all were beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: Among tens of thousands of recruits, none matched him.

sentences.zh: 光將詣行在所，賓客送至灞上者百餘騎。

translations.literal: When Guang was about to go to the imperial camp, more than a hundred mounted guests escorted him as far as Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out for the imperial camp, more than a hundred mounted friends escorted him to Bashang.

sentences.zh: 光酹酒而誓曰：「是行也，若不能建立功名，當死於高麗，不復與諸君相見矣。」

translations.literal: Guang poured a libation of wine and swore: "On this expedition, if I cannot establish merit and fame, I shall die in Goguryeo and never meet you again."
translations.idiomatic: He poured a libation and swore, "On this campaign I will either win glory or die in Goguryeo and never see you again."

sentences.zh: 及從帝攻遼東，以沖梯擊城，竿長十五丈，光升其端，臨城與賊戰，短兵接，殺十數人。

translations.literal: When he followed the emperor in the attack on Liaodong, assault ladders were used against the walls; the pole was fifteen zhang long. Guang climbed to its top, fought the enemy overlooking the wall at close quarters, and killed more than ten men.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he rode a fifteen-zhang assault ladder to the top, fought hand to hand above the wall, and killed more than ten men.

sentences.zh: 賊競擊之而墜，未及於地，適遇竿有垂絙，光接而復上。

translations.literal: The enemy all struck at him and he fell; before he reached the ground he happened upon a hanging rope on the pole, caught it, and climbed up again.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy struck him down, but before he hit the ground he caught a hanging rope on the pole and climbed back up.

sentences.zh: 帝望見，壯異之，馳召與語，大悅，即日拜朝請大夫，賜寶刀良馬，恆致左右，親顧漸密。

translations.literal: The emperor saw it from afar, admired his valor and found it strange, galloped to summon and speak with him, was greatly pleased, and that same day appointed him Court Gentleman for Submission, granted a treasured sword and fine horse, constantly kept him at his side, and drew ever closer in personal regard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw it from afar, was astonished, summoned him, and was delighted. That same day he made him Court Gentleman for Submission, gave him a treasured sword and fine horse, and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以為折衝郎將，賞遇優重。

translations.literal: Before long he was made General Who Breaks the Enemy, with rewards and favor exceptionally heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made General Who Breaks the Enemy, with exceptional rewards and favor.

sentences.zh: 帝每推食解衣以賜之，同輩莫與為比。

translations.literal: The emperor often shared his food and gave him his own garments; none among his peers could be compared with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often shared his food and gave him his own clothes; none among his peers could compare.

sentences.zh: 光自以荷恩深重，思懷竭節。

translations.literal: Guang, considering himself deeply indebted for grace, constantly thought of giving his utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply conscious of the emperor's favor, he was always ready to give his life.

sentences.zh: 及江都之難，潛構義勇，將為帝復仇。

translations.literal: When the disaster at Jiangdu occurred, he secretly organized loyal volunteers, intending to avenge the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck at Jiangdu, he secretly gathered loyal men to avenge the emperor.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝寵昵官奴，名為給使，宇文化及以光驍勇，方任之，令其總統，營于禁內。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had favored palace slaves called "attendants"; Yuwen Huaji, because Guang was fierce and brave, had just then entrusted him, ordering him to command them and camp within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had favored palace slaves called attendants. Yuwen Huaji, trusting Guang's prowess, put him in command of them within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 時孟才、錢傑等陰圖化及，因謂光曰：「我等荷國厚恩，不能死難以衛社稷，斯則古人之所恥也。

translations.literal: At that time Mengcai, Qian Jie, and others were secretly plotting against Huaji and therefore said to Guang: "We owe the state a profound debt of grace; if we cannot die in hardship to defend the altars of state, that is what the ancients would have despised.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai, Qian Jie, and others were secretly plotting against Huaji. They told Guang, "We owe the state everything. To fail to die defending the realm is what the ancients despised.

sentences.zh: 今又俯首事讎，受其驅率，有靦面目，何用生為？

translations.literal: Now we again bow our heads and serve our enemy, driven by him—what face have we left? Of what use is life?
translations.idiomatic: Now we bow to our enemy and take his orders. What face have we left? Why go on living?

sentences.zh: 吾必欲殺之，死無所恨，公義士也，肯從我乎？」

translations.literal: I am determined to kill him and will die without regret. You are a man of righteousness—will you follow me?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to kill him and will die without regret. You are a man of honor—will you join me?"

sentences.zh: 光泣下沾衿，曰：「是所望于將軍也。

translations.literal: Guang wept until his collar was wet and said: "That is what I have hoped for from you, General.
translations.idiomatic: Guang wept until his collar was soaked. "That is what I have hoped for, General.

sentences.zh: 僕領給使數百人，並荷先帝恩遇，今在化及內營。

translations.literal: I command several hundred attendants, all of whom owed favor to the late emperor, and they are now in Huaji's inner camp.
translations.idiomatic: I command several hundred attendants who owed the late emperor everything. They are now in Huaji's inner camp.

sentences.zh: 以此復讎，如鷹鸇之逐鳥雀。

translations.literal: With this to take revenge would be like a hawk or kite pursuing sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: With them we can take revenge as easily as a hawk takes sparrows.

sentences.zh: 萬世之功，在此一舉，願將軍勉之。」

translations.literal: Merit for ten thousand generations rests on this one stroke—I beg the General to exert himself."
translations.idiomatic: Glory for ages rests on this one stroke. I urge you, General, to act."

sentences.zh: 孟才為將軍，領江淮之眾數千人，期以營將發時，晨起襲化及。

translations.literal: Mengcai served as general, leading several thousand men from the Jianghuai region, planning to strike Huaji at dawn when the camp was about to break camp.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai was to lead several thousand men from the Jianghuai region and strike at dawn when the camp broke camp.

sentences.zh: 光語泄，陳謙告其事。

translations.literal: Guang's words leaked out and Chen Qian reported the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked, and Chen Qian reported it.

sentences.zh: 化及大懼曰：「此麥鐵杖子也，及沈光者，並勇決不可當，須避其鋒。」

translations.literal: Huaji was greatly afraid and said: "This is Mai Tiezhang's son, and Shen Guang as well—both are fiercely resolute and cannot be withstood; we must avoid their edge."
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was terrified. "This is Mai Tiezhang's son, and Shen Guang—they are unstoppable. We must avoid them."

sentences.zh: 是夜即與腹心走出營外，留人告司馬德戡等，遣領兵馬，逮捕孟才。

translations.literal: That night he immediately left the camp with his closest followers, left men to inform Sima Dekan and others, and sent troops to arrest Mengcai.
translations.idiomatic: That night he fled the camp with his closest followers, sent word to Sima Dekan, and had troops arrest Mengcai.

sentences.zh: 光聞營內喧聲，知事發，不及被甲，即襲化及營，空無所獲。

translations.literal: Guang heard uproar within the camp, knew the affair had been exposed, had no time to don armor, and immediately attacked Huaji's camp but found it empty and gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing uproar in the camp, Guang knew the plot was exposed. Without armor he attacked Huaji's camp but found it empty.

sentences.zh: 值舍人元敏，數而斬之。

translations.literal: He happened upon Attendant Yuan Min, reviled him repeatedly, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He came upon Attendant Yuan Min, cursed him, and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 遇德戡兵入，四面圍合。

translations.literal: He encountered Dekan's troops entering and was surrounded on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan's troops arrived and surrounded him on all sides.

sentences.zh: 光大呼潰圍，給使齊奮，斬首數十級，賊皆披靡。

translations.literal: Guang shouted and broke through the encirclement; the attendants all fought fiercely together, beheading several dozen men, and the enemy all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Guang shouted and broke through the ring. His attendants fought with him, cut down dozens, and the enemy scattered.

sentences.zh: 德戡輒復遣騎，持弓弩，翼而射之。

translations.literal: Dekan immediately sent cavalry again, bearing bows and crossbows, to shoot at him from the flanks.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan immediately sent cavalry again with bows and crossbows to shoot at him from both sides.

sentences.zh: 光身無介胄，遂為所害。

translations.literal: Guang wore no armor on his body and was thus killed.
translations.idiomatic: Guang wore no armor and was killed.

sentences.zh: 麾下數百人皆鬥而死，一無降者。

translations.literal: Several hundred men under his command all fought to the death; not one surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred men under his command fought to the death; not one surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時年二十八。

translations.literal: He was twenty-eight years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 壯士聞之，莫不為之隕涕。

translations.literal: When brave men heard of it, none failed to shed tears for him.
translations.idiomatic: When brave men heard of it, all wept for him.

sentences.zh: 來護兒，字崇善，江都人也。

translations.literal: Lai Hu'er—Lai Hu'er, courtesy name Chongshan, was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Hu'er was a native of Jiangdu. His courtesy name was Chongshan.

sentences.zh: 幼而卓詭，好立奇節。

translations.literal: From youth he was extraordinary and eccentric, fond of establishing remarkable resolve.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was unusual and bold, eager to prove himself in extraordinary ways.

sentences.zh: 初讀《詩》，至「擊鼓其鏜，踴躍用兵」、「羔裘豹飾，孔武有力」，舍書而歎曰：「大丈夫在世當如是。

translations.literal: When he first read the Book of Odes and came to "The drums beat loudly, leap up to wield arms" and "Lamb's fur trimmed with leopard, greatly martial and strong," he put down the book and sighed: "A great man in this world ought to be like this.
translations.idiomatic: When he first read the Book of Odes and came to the lines about drums sounding for war and warriors clad in leopard-trimmed furs, he put down the book and sighed: "A true man in this world should live like that.

sentences.zh: 會為國滅賊以取功名，安能區區久事隴畝！」

translations.literal: One should destroy the enemy for the state and win fame and merit—how could one humbly plow the fields forever!"
translations.idiomatic: He should destroy the state's enemies and win glory—how could he spend his life plowing fields!"

sentences.zh: 群輩驚其言而壯其志。

translations.literal: His companions were startled by his words but admired his ambition.
translations.idiomatic: His companions were startled by his words but admired his ambition.

sentences.zh: 護兒所住白土村，密邇江岸。

translations.literal: Hu'er lived in Baitu Village, close to the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er lived in Baitu Village, right by the river.

sentences.zh: 于時江南尚阻，賀若弼之鎮壽州也，常令護兒為間諜，授大都督。

translations.literal: At that time the south of the Yangtze was still blocked. When He Ruo Bi was stationed at Shouzhou, he often used Hu'er as a spy and appointed him Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The south of the Yangtze was still cut off. When He Ruo Bi was stationed at Shouzhou, he often used Hu'er as a spy and made him Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，護兒有功焉，進位上開府。

translations.literal: In the campaign to conquer Chen, Hu'er rendered meritorious service and was promoted to Senior General of the Opening Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign to conquer Chen, Hu'er distinguished himself and was promoted to Senior General of the Opening Gate.

sentences.zh: 從楊素擊高智慧於浙江，而賊據岸為營，周亙百餘里，船艦被江，鼓噪而進。

translations.literal: Following Yang Su he attacked Gao Zhihui on the Zhe River. The rebels held the shore and established camps stretching more than a hundred li in circumference; their ships covered the river as they advanced with drums and shouts.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yang Su to attack Gao Zhihui on the Zhe River. The rebels held the shore in camps stretching more than a hundred li; their ships filled the river as they advanced with drums and battle cries.

sentences.zh: 素令護兒率數百輕艓徑登江岸，直掩其營，破之。

translations.literal: Su ordered Hu'er to lead several hundred light boats directly up to the riverbank and strike their camp at once, breaking it.
translations.idiomatic: Su ordered Hu'er to lead several hundred light boats straight to the riverbank and storm their camp, breaking it.

sentences.zh: 時賊前與素戰不勝，歸無所據，因而潰散。

translations.literal: The rebels had earlier fought Su without victory and had nowhere to return; they therefore dissolved in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already been defeated by Su and had nowhere to regroup, so they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 智慧將逃於海，護兒追至泉州，智慧窮蹙，遁走閩、越。

translations.literal: Zhihui was about to flee to the sea. Hu'er pursued him to Quanzhou; Zhihui, in dire straits, fled into Min and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui tried to flee to the sea. Hu'er pursued him to Quanzhou; cornered, Zhihui escaped into Min and Yue.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍，除泉州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Great General and appointed Prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Great General and appointed Prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時有盛道延擁兵作亂，侵擾州境，護兒進擊，破之。

translations.literal: At that time Sheng Daoyan raised troops in rebellion and harassed the prefecture. Hu'er advanced against him and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sheng Daoyan raised troops in rebellion and raided the prefecture. Hu'er attacked and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 又從蒲山公李寬破汪文進於黟、歙，進位柱國，

translations.literal: He also followed Duke of Pusan Li Kuan to defeat Wang Wenjin at Yi and She, and was promoted to Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed the Duke of Pusan, Li Kuan, to defeat Wang Wenjin at Yi and She, and was promoted to Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 仁壽三年，除瀛州刺史，賜爵黃縣公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Renshou, he was appointed Prefect of Yingzhou, granted the title Duke of Huang County with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Renshou, he was appointed Prefect of Yingzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Huang County with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋加上柱國，除右禦衛將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Senior Pillar of the State and appointed General of the Right Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Senior Pillar of the State and appointed General of the Right Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷右驍衛大將軍，帝甚親重之，

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Hu'er was transferred to Great General of the Right Valiant Guard; the Emperor held him in close favor and high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Hu'er was made Great General of the Right Valiant Guard, and the Emperor favored and trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 大業六年，從駕江都，賜物千段，令上先人塚，宴父老，州裡榮之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daye, he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu, was granted a thousand bolts of goods, and was ordered to visit his ancestors' tombs and feast the elders of the district—the whole region took pride in it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daye, he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu, received a thousand bolts of goods, and was sent to visit his ancestors' tombs and feast the local elders—a great honor for the whole district.

sentences.zh: 數歲，轉右翊衛大將軍。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to Great General of the Right Imposing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was transferred to Great General of the Right Imposing Guard.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，護兒率樓船，指滄海，入自壩水，去平壤六十里，與高麗相遇。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign, Hu'er led tower ships toward the eastern sea, entered by the Banshui route, and was sixty li from Pyongyang when he met the Goguryeo forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign, Hu'er led tower ships toward the eastern sea, entered by the Banshui route, and met Goguryeo forces sixty li from Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 進擊，大破之，乘勝直造城下，破其郛郭。

translations.literal: He pressed the attack and routed them, then following his victory went straight to the city walls and broke through the outer defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack, routed them, and following his victory drove straight to the city and broke through the outer walls.

sentences.zh: 於是縱軍大掠，稍失部伍，高元弟建武募敢死士五百人邀擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he let his troops plunder freely and his ranks fell somewhat out of order. Gao Yuan's brother Jianwu recruited five hundred dare-to-die men to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: He then let his troops plunder freely and his ranks fell out of order. Gao Yuan's brother Jianwu recruited five hundred dare-to-die men to ambush him.

sentences.zh: 護兒因卻，屯營海浦，以待期會。

translations.literal: Hu'er therefore withdrew and encamped on the seashore, awaiting the scheduled rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er withdrew and encamped on the coast, waiting for the planned rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 後知宇文述等敗，遂班師。

translations.literal: Later, learning that Yuwen Shu and the others had been defeated, he withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Later, learning that Yuwen Shu and the others had been defeated, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，又出滄海道，師次東萊，會楊玄感作逆黎陽，進逼鞏、洛，護兒勒兵與宇文述等擊破之。

translations.literal: The next year he set out again by the eastern sea route. His army halted at Donglai when Yang Xuangan rebelled at Liyang and pressed toward Gong and Luo. Hu'er mustered his troops and, with Yuwen Shu and others, defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he set out again by the eastern sea route. His army halted at Donglai when Yang Xuangan rebelled at Liyang and pressed toward Gong and Luoyang. Hu'er mustered his troops and, with Yuwen Shu and others, defeated him.

sentences.zh: 封榮國公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Rong with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Rong with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 十年，又帥師度海，至卑奢城，高麗舉國來戰，護兒大破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again led his army across the sea to Beishe City. Goguryeo mustered its whole nation to fight; Hu'er routed them and took more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he again led his army across the sea to Beishe City. Goguryeo mustered its whole nation to fight; Hu'er routed them and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 將趣平壤，高元震懼，遣使執叛臣斛斯政，詣遼東城下，上表請降。

translations.literal: As he was about to advance on Pyongyang, Gao Yuan was terrified and sent envoys to bring the rebel minister Qie Sizheng to the walls of Liaodong and submit a memorial begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to advance on Pyongyang, Gao Yuan was terrified. He sent envoys to bring the rebel minister Qie Sizheng to the walls of Liaodong and submit a memorial begging to surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，遣人持節詔護兒旋師。

translations.literal: The Emperor consented and sent an envoy bearing imperial credentials ordering Hu'er to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed and sent an envoy with imperial credentials ordering Hu'er to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 護兒集眾曰：「三度出兵，未能平賊，此還也，不可重來。

translations.literal: Hu'er assembled his men and said: "Three times we have marched out and failed to subdue the enemy. If we return now, we cannot come again.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er assembled his men and said: "Three times we have marched out and failed to subdue the enemy. If we go back now, we may never come again.

sentences.zh: 今高麗困弊，野無青草，以我眾戰，不日克之。

translations.literal: Goguryeo is now exhausted; the fields have no green grass. With our numbers in battle, we will conquer them within days.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo is exhausted now; the fields have no green grass. With our numbers we can crush them in days.

sentences.zh: 吾欲進兵，徑圍平壤，取其偽主，獻捷而歸。」

translations.literal: I wish to advance, surround Pyongyang directly, capture their false ruler, and return in triumph."
translations.idiomatic: I want to advance, surround Pyongyang directly, capture their false king, and return in triumph."

sentences.zh: 答表請行，不肯奉詔。

translations.literal: He replied to the memorial requesting permission to proceed and refused to obey the decree.
translations.idiomatic: He replied to the memorial asking permission to advance and refused to obey the decree.

sentences.zh: 長史崔君肅固爭，不許。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Cui Junsu argued against it firmly and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Cui Junsu argued against it firmly and would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 護兒曰：」賊勢破矣，專以相任，自足辦之。

translations.literal: Hu'er said: "The enemy's strength is broken. You have entrusted everything to me alone; that is enough to finish the job.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er said: "The enemy is broken. You have put me in sole command—that is enough to finish this.

sentences.zh: 吾在閫外，事合專決，豈容千里稟聽成規！

translations.literal: I am beyond the passes; matters ought to be decided on my own authority. How can I wait a thousand li for approval of a fixed plan!
translations.idiomatic: I am beyond the frontier; I must decide on my own. How can I wait a thousand li for orders on a plan already set!

sentences.zh: 俄頃之間，動失機會，勞而無功，故其宜也。

translations.literal: In the blink of an eye one loses the opportunity; labor without success—that is why independent command at the frontier is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In an instant the chance is lost and all the labor comes to nothing—that is why a commander at the frontier must decide for himself.

sentences.zh: 吾甯征得高元，還而獲譴，舍此成功，所不能矣。」

translations.literal: I would rather capture Gao Yuan and face punishment on my return than abandon this success—I cannot do that."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather capture Gao Yuan and face punishment when I return than give up this victory—I cannot do that."

sentences.zh: 君肅告眾曰：「若從元帥，違拒詔書，必當聞奏，皆獲罪也。」

translations.literal: Junsu told the assembly: "If we follow the Marshal and disobey the imperial decree, I must report it, and all will be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Junsu told the assembly: "If we follow the Marshal and disobey the imperial decree, I must report it, and all of us will be punished."

sentences.zh: 諸將懼，盡勸還，方始奉詔。

translations.literal: The generals were afraid and all urged withdrawal; only then did he obey the decree.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were afraid and all urged withdrawal; only then did he obey the decree.

sentences.zh: 十三年，轉為左翊衛大將軍，進位開府儀同三司，任委逾密，前後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Great General of the Left Imposing Guard and promoted to Grand Master of the Opening Gate with the ceremonial rank of the Three Preceptors. His duties grew ever more confidential, and rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Great General of the Left Imposing Guard and promoted to Grand Master of the Opening Gate with the ceremonial rank of the Three Preceptors. His responsibilities grew ever closer, and the rewards he received were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 江都之難，宇文化及忌而害之。

translations.literal: At the catastrophe at Jiangdu, Yuwen Huaji killed him out of jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: At the catastrophe at Jiangdu, Yuwen Huaji killed him out of jealousy.

sentences.zh: 長子楷，以父軍功授散騎郎、朝散大夫。

translations.literal: His eldest son Kai, on account of his father's military merit, was appointed Gentleman Attendant-at-Large and Grand Master for Governing the Court.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Kai, on account of his father's military merit, was appointed Gentleman Attendant-at-Large and Grand Master for Governing the Court.

sentences.zh: 楷弟弘，仕至果毅郎將、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Hong rose to the posts of Brigadier General of Righteous Courage and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Traces.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's younger brother Hong rose to Brigadier General of Righteous Courage and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Traces.

sentences.zh: 弘第整，武賁郎將、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Zheng was a Commander of the Martial Guard and Grand Master of the Right Light Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's younger brother Zheng was a Commander of the Martial Guard and Grand Master of the Right Light Chariot.

sentences.zh: 整尤驍勇，善撫士眾，討擊群盜，所向皆捷。

translations.literal: Zheng was especially fierce and brave, skilled at winning over his troops; when he attacked bandits he prevailed wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was especially fierce and brave, skilled at winning over his troops. When he attacked bandits he prevailed wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 諸賊甚憚之，為作歌曰：「長白山頭百戰場，十十五五把長槍，不畏官軍十萬眾，只畏榮公第六郎。」

translations.literal: The bandits greatly feared him and made a song: "On Changbai Mountain is a battlefield of a hundred battles; ten here, five there, they grasp long spears. They fear not a hundred thousand government troops—they fear only the Duke of Rong's sixth son."
