translations.idiomatic: The bandits greatly feared him and made up a song: "On Changbai Mountain, battlefield of a hundred fights, ten here and five there with long spears—they fear not a hundred thousand government troops, they fear only the Duke of Rong's sixth son."

sentences.zh: 化及反，皆遇害，唯少子恆、濟獲免。

translations.literal: When Huaji rebelled, they were all killed; only the youngest sons Heng and Ji escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji rebelled, they were all killed; only the youngest sons Heng and Ji escaped.

sentences.zh: 魚俱羅，馮翊下邦人也。

translations.literal: Yu Juluo—Yu Juluo was a native of Xiabang in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Juluo was a native of Xiabang in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，膂力絕人，聲氣雄壯，言聞數百步。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi tall, his strength was unrivaled, his voice was powerful and imposing, and his words could be heard hundreds of paces away.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall, with unmatched strength, a powerful voice, and words that carried for hundreds of paces.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為親衛，累遷大都督。

translations.literal: At twenty he served in the Imperial Guard and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered the Imperial Guard and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 從晉王廣平陳，以功拜開府，賜物一千五百段。

translations.literal: Following Prince of Jin Guang in the conquest of Chen, he was made General of the Opening Gate for his service and granted fifteen hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Guang of Jin in the conquest of Chen, was made General of the Opening Gate for his service, and received fifteen hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 未幾，沈玄懀、高智慧等作亂江南，楊素以俱羅壯勇，請與同行。

translations.literal: Before long Shen Xuanchi, Gao Zhihui, and others raised rebellion in the south. Yang Su, considering Juluo's valor, requested that he go with him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shen Xuanchi, Gao Zhihui, and others rebelled in the south. Yang Su, impressed by Juluo's valor, asked that he come along.

sentences.zh: 每戰有功，加上開府、高唐縣公，拜疊州總管。

translations.literal: In every battle he performed with merit. He was made Senior General of the Opening Gate and Duke of Gaotang County, and appointed Area Commander of Diezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in every battle and was made Senior General of the Opening Gate and Duke of Gaotang County, then appointed Area Commander of Diezhou.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 還至扶風，會楊素率兵將出靈州道擊突厥，路逢俱羅，大悅，遂奏與同行。

translations.literal: Returning to Fufeng, he met Yang Su leading troops about to set out by the Lingzhou route against the Turks. Su was greatly pleased, had him join the campaign, and memorialized for permission to bring him along.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back to Fufeng he met Yang Su leading troops out by the Lingzhou route against the Turks. Su was delighted, took him along, and memorialized for permission.

sentences.zh: 及遇賊，俱羅與數騎奔擊，瞋目大呼，所當皆披靡，出左入右，往返若飛。

translations.literal: When they met the enemy, Juluo charged with a few horsemen, glared and shouted; all who faced him broke and fled. He darted left and right, back and forth like flight.
translations.idiomatic: When they met the enemy, Juluo charged with a few horsemen, glaring and shouting. All who faced him broke and fled as he darted left and right like lightning.

sentences.zh: 以功進位柱國，拜豐州總管。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Pillar of the State and appointed Area Commander of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Pillar of the State and appointed Area Commander of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥數入境為寇，俱羅輒擒斬之，自是突厥畏懼屏跡，不敢畜牧於塞上。

translations.literal: At first the Turks repeatedly crossed the border to raid. Juluo always captured and executed them; from then on the Turks were afraid and withdrew from sight, not daring to graze livestock along the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Turks repeatedly crossed the border to raid. Juluo always captured and executed them, and from then on the Turks were afraid and vanished from the frontier, not daring to graze their herds there.

sentences.zh: 初，煬帝在籓，俱羅弟贊以左右從，累遷大都督。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Yang was still a prince, Juluo's younger brother Zan followed him as an attendant and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Yang was still a prince, Juluo's younger brother Zan served at his side and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 及帝嗣位，拜車騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor succeeded to the throne, Zan was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor succeeded to the throne, Zan was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 贊性凶暴，虐其部下，令左右炙肉，遇不中意，以簽刺瞎其眼。

translations.literal: Zan was cruel and violent by nature and tyrannized his subordinates. He had his attendants roast meat; if it displeased him, he stabbed out their eyes with a skewer.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was cruel and violent and tyrannized his subordinates. He had attendants roast meat for him; if it displeased him, he stabbed out their eyes with a skewer.

sentences.zh: 有溫酒不適者，立斷其舌。

translations.literal: If anyone warmed wine unsatisfactorily, he instantly cut out his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone warmed wine to his displeasure, he instantly cut out the man's tongue.

sentences.zh: 帝以贊籓邸之舊，不忍加誅，謂近臣曰：「弟既如此，兄亦可知。」

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Zan was an old companion from the princely household, could not bear to execute him. He said to close ministers: "If the younger brother is like this, one can guess what the elder is like."
translations.idiomatic: Because Zan had been with him since his days as prince, the Emperor could not bear to execute him. He told close ministers: "If the younger brother is like this, one can guess what the elder is like."

sentences.zh: 因召俱羅，譴責之，出贊於獄，令自為計。

translations.literal: He thereupon summoned Juluo, rebuked him, released Zan from prison, and told him to decide his own fate.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Juluo and rebuked him, released Zan from prison, and told him to decide his own fate.

sentences.zh: 贊至家，飲藥而死。

translations.literal: Zan went home and died by poison.
translations.idiomatic: Zan went home and took poison.

sentences.zh: 帝恐俱羅不自安，慮生邊患，轉為安州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared Juluo would feel insecure and that trouble might arise on the frontier, so he transferred him to Prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor feared Juluo would feel insecure and that trouble might arise on the frontier, so he transferred him to Prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷趙郡太守。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Governor of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to Governor of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後因朝集，至東都，與將軍梁伯隱有舊，數相往來。

translations.literal: Later, on account of the annual court assembly, he came to the Eastern Capital and had old ties with General Liang Boyin; they visited each other often.
translations.idiomatic: Later, coming to the Eastern Capital for the annual court assembly, he renewed old ties with General Liang Boyin and they visited each other often.

sentences.zh: 又從郡多將雜物以貢獻，帝不受，因遺權貴。

translations.literal: He also brought many assorted goods from his commandery as tribute. The Emperor would not accept them, so he gave them to powerful officials instead.
translations.idiomatic: He also brought many assorted goods from his commandery as tribute. The Emperor refused them, so he gave them to powerful officials instead.

sentences.zh: 御史劾俱羅以郡將交通內臣，帝大怒，與伯隱俱坐除名。

translations.literal: Censors impeached Juluo for a frontier commander dealing with palace officials. The Emperor was furious, and both Juluo and Boyin were stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached Juluo for a frontier commander consorting with palace officials. The Emperor was furious, and both Juluo and Boyin were stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，越巂飛山蠻作亂，侵掠郡境。

translations.literal: Before long the Feishan tribes of Yuexi rebelled and raided the commandery borders.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Feishan tribes of Yuexi rebelled and raided the commandery.

sentences.zh: 詔俱羅白衣領將，並率蜀郡都尉段鐘葵討平之，

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Juluo, though stripped of rank, to lead troops, together with Duan Zhongkui, Commandant of Shu Commandery, to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Juluo, though stripped of rank, to lead troops with Duan Zhongkui, Commandant of Shu Commandery, to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 大業九年，重征高麗，以俱羅為碣石道軍將。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye, on the renewed campaign against Goguryeo, Juluo was made army commander of the Jieshi route.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daye, on the renewed campaign against Goguryeo, Juluo was made army commander of the Jieshi route.

sentences.zh: 及還，江南劉元進作亂，詔俱羅將兵向會稽諸郡逐捕之。

translations.literal: When he returned, Liu Yuanjin rebelled in the south. The Emperor ordered Juluo to lead troops into the commanderies around Kuaiji to pursue and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, Liu Yuanjin rebelled in the south. The Emperor ordered Juluo to lead troops through the Kuaiji commanderies to pursue and capture him.

sentences.zh: 于時百姓思亂，從盜如市，俱羅擊賊帥朱燮、管崇等，戰無不捷。

translations.literal: At that time the people were eager for rebellion and joined bandits as if at a market. Juluo attacked the bandit chiefs Zhu Xie, Guan Chong, and others and was victorious in every battle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people were eager for rebellion and joined bandits as if at a market. Juluo attacked the bandit chiefs Zhu Xie, Guan Chong, and others and won every battle.

sentences.zh: 然賊勢浸盛，敗而復聚。

translations.literal: Yet the rebels' strength kept growing; defeated, they regathered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebels kept growing stronger; defeated, they regathered.

sentences.zh: 俱羅度賊非歲月可平，諸子並在京、洛，又見天下漸亂，終恐道路隔絕。

translations.literal: Juluo judged that the rebels could not be subdued in months. His sons were all in the capital region, and seeing the realm growing chaotic, he finally feared the roads would be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Juluo judged that the rebels could not be subdued in months. His sons were all in the capital, and as the realm grew chaotic he feared the roads would be cut off.

sentences.zh: 于時東都饑饉，穀食踴貴，俱羅遣家僕將船米至東都糶之，益市財貨，潛迎諸子。

translations.literal: At that time the Eastern Capital suffered famine and grain prices soared. Juluo sent household servants with boats of rice to sell in the Eastern Capital, bought more goods, and secretly brought his sons south.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital was starving and grain prices soared. Juluo sent household servants with boatloads of rice to sell there, bought more goods, and secretly brought his sons south.

sentences.zh: 朝廷微知之，恐其有異志，發使案驗。

translations.literal: The court learned of this in part and, fearing disloyal intent, sent envoys to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The court learned of this in part and, fearing disloyal intent, sent envoys to investigate.

sentences.zh: 使者至，前後察問，不得其罪。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived and questioned him repeatedly, they found no crime.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived and questioned him repeatedly, they found no crime.

sentences.zh: 帝復令大理司直梁敬真就鎖將詣東都。

translations.literal: The Emperor again ordered Liang Jingzhen, Direct Inspector of the Court of Judicature, to go to him in shackles and escort him to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again ordered Liang Jingzhen, Direct Inspector of the Court of Judicature, to go to him in shackles and escort him to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 俱羅相表異人，目有重瞳，陰為帝之所忌。

translations.literal: Juluo looked like an extraordinary man and had double pupils in his eyes; secretly the Emperor resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Juluo looked like an extraordinary man and had double pupils in his eyes; secretly the Emperor resented this.

sentences.zh: 敬真希旨，奏俱羅師徒敗衄，於是斬東都市，家口籍沒。

translations.literal: Jingzhen, following the Emperor's intent, memorialized that Juluo's army had been defeated. He was then executed in the Eastern Capital market, and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen, following the Emperor's intent, memorialized that Juluo's army had been defeated. Juluo was executed in the Eastern Capital market, and his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 陳棱，字長威，廬江襄安人也。

translations.literal: Chen Leng—Chen Leng, courtesy name Changwei, was a native of Xiang'an in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Leng was a native of Xiang'an in Lujiang. His courtesy name was Changwei.

sentences.zh: 祖碩，以漁釣自給。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuo supported himself by fishing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuo made his living by fishing.

sentences.zh: 父峴，少驍勇，事章大寶為帳內部曲。

translations.literal: His father Xian was fierce and brave in youth and served Zhang Dabao as a personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian was fierce and brave in youth and served Zhang Dabao as a personal guard.

sentences.zh: 告大寶反，授譙州刺史。

translations.literal: He reported Dabao's rebellion and was appointed Prefect of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He reported Dabao's rebellion and was appointed Prefect of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 陳滅，廢於家。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he was retired at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he was retired at home.

sentences.zh: 高智慧、汪文進等作亂江南，廬江豪傑亦舉兵相應，以峴舊將，共推為主。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui, Wang Wenjin, and others rebelled in the south, the heroes of Lujiang also raised troops in response. Because Xian was a former general, they jointly made him their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui, Wang Wenjin, and others rebelled in the south, the heroes of Lujiang also raised troops in response. Because Xian was a former general, they made him their leader.

sentences.zh: 峴欲拒之，棱謂峴曰：「眾亂既作，拒之禍且及己。

translations.literal: Xian wished to refuse. Leng said to Xian: "Once the mass rebellion has begun, refusing will bring disaster on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Xian wished to refuse. Leng said to him: "Once rebellion has broken out everywhere, refusing will bring disaster on you.

sentences.zh: 不如偽從，別為後計。」

translations.literal: Better to pretend to join them and plan separately for what comes next."
translations.idiomatic: Better to pretend to join them and plan for what comes next."

sentences.zh: 峴然之。

translations.literal: Xian agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xian agreed.

sentences.zh: 時柱國李徹軍至當塗，峴潛使棱至徹所，請為內應。

translations.literal: At that time Pillar of the State Li Che's army reached Dangtu. Xian secretly sent Leng to Che's camp to offer to serve as an inside contact.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Che, Pillar of the State, reached Dangtu with his army. Xian secretly sent Leng to Che's camp to offer to serve as an inside contact.

sentences.zh: 徹上其事，拜上大將軍、宣州刺史，封譙郡公，邑一千戶，詔徹應接之。

translations.literal: Che reported the matter upward. [Xian] was appointed Grand General and Prefect of Xuanzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao Commandery with a fief of one thousand households, and an edict ordered Che to coordinate the response.
translations.idiomatic: Che reported the affair to the court. Xian was made Grand General and Prefect of Xuanzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao Commandery with a fief of one thousand households, and an edict ordered Che to coordinate with him.

sentences.zh: 徹軍未至，謀泄，為其黨所殺，棱僅以獲免。

translations.literal: Before Che's army arrived, the plot leaked. [Xian] was killed by his own faction, and Leng narrowly escaped capture.
translations.idiomatic: Before Che's army arrived, the plot was discovered. Xian was killed by his own followers, and Leng barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 上以其父之故，拜開府，尋領鄉兵。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of his father's [merit], appointed him General of the Opening Gate. Before long he took command of local militia.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his father's service, the Emperor made him General of the Opening Gate. Before long he took command of local militia.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，授驃騎將軍，

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he was appointed General of Fast Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was appointed General of Fast Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，拜武賁郎將。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, he was also appointed Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye, he was also made Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 後三歲，與朝請大夫張鎮周發東陽兵萬餘人，自義安泛海，擊流求國，月餘而至。

translations.literal: Three years later, together with Palace Attendant Zhang Zhenzhou, he mobilized more than ten thousand troops from Dongyang, sailed from Yi'an across the sea to attack the kingdom of Liuqiu, and arrived after a little more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, together with Palace Attendant Zhang Zhenzhou, he raised more than ten thousand troops from Dongyang, sailed from Yi'an across the sea against the kingdom of Liuqiu, and arrived after a little over a month.

sentences.zh: 流求人初見船艦，以為商旅，往往詣軍中貿易。

translations.literal: When the people of Liuqiu first saw the ships, they took them for merchant vessels and often came to the army camp to trade.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Liuqiu first saw the fleet, they took it for a merchant convoy and often came to the camp to trade.

sentences.zh: 棱率眾登岸，遣鎮周為先鋒。

translations.literal: Leng led his troops ashore and sent Zhenzhou as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Leng led his men ashore and sent Zhenzhou ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 其主歡斯渴剌兜遣兵拒戰，鎮周頻擊破之。

translations.literal: Their ruler Huansikoulou sent troops to resist. Zhenzhou repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Their king Huansikoulou sent troops to meet them, and Zhenzhou beat them again and again.

sentences.zh: 棱進至低沒檀洞，其小王歡斯老模率兵拒戰，棱擊敗之，斬老模。

translations.literal: Leng advanced to Dimotan Cave. The lesser king Huansilaomo led troops to resist. Leng defeated them and beheaded Laomo.
translations.idiomatic: Leng pushed on to Dimotan Cave. The lesser king Huansilaomo fought him, but Leng broke his force and took Laomo's head.

sentences.zh: 其日霧雨晦冥，將士皆懼，棱刑白馬以祭海神。

translations.literal: That day fog and rain made the sky dark. The officers and soldiers were all afraid. Leng executed a white horse to sacrifice to the Sea God.
translations.idiomatic: That day fog and rain blotted out the sky, and the officers and soldiers were afraid. Leng sacrificed a white horse to the Sea God.

sentences.zh: 既而開霽，分為五軍，趣其都邑。

translations.literal: Before long the sky cleared. [They] divided into five armies and pressed toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the weather cleared. They divided into five armies and pressed on toward the enemy capital.

sentences.zh: 渴剌兜率眾數千逆拒，棱遣鎮周又先鋒擊走之。

translations.literal: Koulou led several thousand men to meet them in resistance. Leng again sent Zhenzhou as vanguard to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Koulou led several thousand men out to oppose them. Leng again sent Zhenzhou ahead, and he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 棱乘勝逐北，至其柵，渴剌兜背柵而陣。

translations.literal: Leng pursued the fleeing enemy in victory, reaching their palisade. Koulou turned his back to the palisade and formed battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Leng pursued the fleeing enemy to their palisade. Koulou turned his back to the stockade and drew up his battle line.

sentences.zh: 棱盡銳擊之，從辰至未，苦鬥不息。

translations.literal: Leng deployed all his elite troops to attack. From the hour chen to the hour wei, they fought bitterly without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Leng threw all his best troops into the attack. From the hour chen to the hour wei they fought without letup.

sentences.zh: 渴剌兜自以軍疲，引入柵。

translations.literal: Koulou, judging his army exhausted, withdrew into the palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Koulou, seeing his army exhausted, withdrew behind the stockade.

sentences.zh: 棱遂填塹，攻破其柵，斬渴剌兜，獲其子島槌，虜男女數千而歸。

translations.literal: Leng then filled the moat, broke through the palisade, beheaded Koulou, captured his son Daosui, and returned with several thousand men and women as captives.
translations.idiomatic: Leng filled the moat, broke through the stockade, beheaded Koulou, captured his son Daosui, and returned with several thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，進棱位右光祿大夫，武賁如故，鎮周金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased. Leng was promoted to Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, retaining his Martial Guard post. Zhenzhou was made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Traces.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased. Leng was promoted to Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness while keeping his Martial Guard post, and Zhenzhou was made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Traces.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以宿衛遷左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign, because of his palace guard service he was transferred to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, his service in the palace guard earned him promotion to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復征遼東，棱為東萊留守。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor again marched on Liaodong. Leng served as garrison commander of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Emperor marched on Liaodong again, and Leng was left to hold Donglai.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之作亂也，棱率眾萬餘人擊平黎陽，斬玄感所署刺史元務本。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Leng led more than ten thousand men, attacked and pacified Liyang, and beheaded Yuan Wuben, the prefect Yang Xuangan had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Leng led more than ten thousand men, recaptured Liyang, and beheaded Yuan Wuben, the prefect Xuangan had installed.

sentences.zh: 棱尋奉詔于江南營戰艦。

translations.literal: Before long Leng received orders to build warships in the Jiangnan region.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Leng received orders to build warships in the south.

sentences.zh: 至彭城，賊帥孟讓眾將十萬，據都梁宮，阻淮為固。

translations.literal: At Pengcheng, the bandit chief Meng Rang and his generals numbered one hundred thousand. They occupied Duliang Palace and fortified themselves against the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengcheng the bandit chief Meng Rang commanded one hundred thousand men. He seized Duliang Palace and used the Huai River as his defense.

sentences.zh: 棱潛於下流而濟，至江都，率兵襲讓，破之。

translations.literal: Leng secretly crossed at a lower ford, reached Jiangdu, and led troops in a surprise attack on Rang, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Leng secretly crossed farther downstream, reached Jiangdu, and led a surprise attack that broke Meng Rang.

sentences.zh: 以功進位光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 賜爵信安侯。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 後帝幸江都宮，俄而李子通據海陵，左才相掠淮北，杜伏威屯六合，眾各數萬。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor visited Jiangdu Palace. Before long Li Zitong seized Hailing; Zuo Caixiang plundered north of the Huai; Du Fuwei was encamped at Liuhe — each with forces numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Emperor went to Jiangdu Palace. Before long Li Zitong seized Hailing, Zuo Caixiang raided north of the Huai, and Du Fuwei held Liuhe — each with an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 帝遣棱率宿衛兵擊之，往往克捷。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Leng to lead the palace guard troops against them. He repeatedly won victories.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Leng with the palace guard against them, and he won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 超拜右禦衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was abruptly promoted to General of the Right Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was suddenly promoted to General of the Right Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 復渡清江，擊宣城賊。

translations.literal: He again crossed the Qing River and attacked the bandits of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Qing River again and attacked the bandits around Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝以弑崩，宇文化及引軍北上，召棱守江都。

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor died by assassination. Yuwen Huaji led his army north and summoned Leng to guard Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Emperor was assassinated. Yuwen Huaji marched north and ordered Leng to hold Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 棱集眾縞素，為煬帝發喪，備儀衛，改葬于吳公台下，衰杖送喪，慟感行路，論者深義之。

translations.literal: Leng gathered the troops in white hemp mourning dress, held funeral rites for Emperor Yang, deployed the full guard of honor, and reburied him below Wugong Terrace. Wearing mourning garments and leaning on staves, they escorted the coffin. Their grief moved passersby on the road, and commentators deeply praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Leng gathered his men in white mourning dress, held funeral rites for Emperor Yang, mustered the full guard of honor, and reburied him below Wugong Terrace. Clad in mourning and leaning on staves, they escorted the coffin. Their grief moved everyone on the road, and commentators praised his righteousness in the highest terms.

sentences.zh: 棱後為李子通所陷，奔杜伏威，伏威忌之，尋而見害。

translations.literal: Leng was later entrapped by Li Zitong, fled to Du Fuwei, and Fuwei resented him. Before long Leng was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Leng was later framed by Li Zitong and fled to Du Fuwei, but Fuwei resented him and soon had him killed.

sentences.zh: 王辯，字警略，馮翊蒲城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Bian—Wang Bian, courtesy name Jinglue, was a native of Pucheng in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bian was a native of Pucheng in Fengyi. His courtesy name was Jinglue.

sentences.zh: 祖訓，以行商致富。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xun grew wealthy through commerce.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xun grew wealthy as a merchant.

sentences.zh: 魏世，出粟助給軍糧，為假清河太守。

translations.literal: In the Wei era he contributed grain to supply the army and was made Acting Prefect of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he contributed grain to supply the army and was made Acting Prefect of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 辯少習兵書，尤善騎射，慷慨有大志。

translations.literal: Bian in youth studied military texts and was especially skilled at mounted archery. He was generous and had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Bian studied military texts and was especially skilled at mounted archery. He was generous and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 在周以軍功授帥都督。

translations.literal: Under Zhou he was appointed Commander-in-Chief for his military merits.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Zhou he was made Commander-in-Chief for his military service.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，遷大都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was transferred to Great Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era he was promoted to Great Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，遷車騎將軍。

translations.literal: During Renshou he was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒之作亂也，從楊素討平之，賜爵武寧縣男，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, [Bian] followed Yang Su in suppressing the rebellion and was granted the title Baron of Wuning with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Han rebelled, Bian followed Yang Su in putting down the revolt and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wuning with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後三歲，遷尚舍奉御。

translations.literal: Three years later he was transferred to Director of Palace Supplies Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was made Director of Palace Supplies Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，拜朝請大夫。

translations.literal: On campaign against Tuyuhun he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Tuyuhun he was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 數年，轉鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to Yingyang Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was made Yingyang Colonel.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以功加通議大夫，尋遷武賁郎將。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign, for merit he was promoted to General Discussion Master, and before long transferred to Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign his service earned him promotion to General Discussion Master, and before long he was made Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 及山東盜賊起，上谷魏刀兒自號曆山飛，眾十餘萬，劫掠燕、趙。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Shandong, Wei Dao'er of Shanggu styled himself Flying over Mount Lishan. His forces numbered more than one hundred thousand, and they plundered Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Shandong, Wei Dao'er of Shanggu styled himself Flying over Mount Lishan. His army numbered more than one hundred thousand, and they ravaged Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 帝引辯升禦榻，問以方略。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Bian ascend the imperial couch and questioned him on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Bian come up to the imperial couch and questioned him about strategy.

sentences.zh: 辯論取賊形勢，帝稱善，曰：「誠如此計，賊何足憂也。」

translations.literal: Bian analyzed how to take the bandits and laid out their strategic situation. The Emperor praised him, saying: "If we truly follow this plan, the bandits are nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Bian explained how to take the bandits and laid out their situation. The Emperor praised him and said, "If we truly follow this plan, the bandits are nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 於是發從行步騎三千，擊敗之，賜黃金二百兩。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched three thousand infantry and cavalry from his entourage. [Bian] defeated them and was granted two hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent three thousand infantry and cavalry from his entourage with Bian, who defeated the bandits and received two hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 明年，渤海賊帥高士達自號東海公，眾以萬數。

translations.literal: The next year the Bohai bandit chief Gao Shida styled himself Duke of the Eastern Sea. His followers numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Bohai bandit chief Gao Shida styled himself Duke of the Eastern Sea, and his followers numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 復令辯擊之，屢挫其銳。

translations.literal: [The Emperor] again ordered Bian to attack him and repeatedly blunted his momentum.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again ordered Bian against him, and Bian repeatedly blunted his momentum.

sentences.zh: 帝在江都宮，聞而馳召之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was at Jiangdu Palace. Upon hearing [of his victories], he urgently summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was at Jiangdu Palace. When he heard of Bian's victories, he urgently summoned him.

sentences.zh: 及引見，禮賜甚厚，復令往信都經略。

translations.literal: When [Bian] was received in audience, the courtesies and rewards were very generous. [The Emperor] again ordered him to go to Xindu to oversee military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian was received in audience, the honors and rewards were lavish. The Emperor again sent him to Xindu to oversee operations.

sentences.zh: 士達於是復戰，破之，優詔褒顯。

translations.literal: Shida then resumed fighting. [Bian] defeated him and received an imperial edict of lavish praise.
translations.idiomatic: Shida then gave battle again, but Bian broke him and received an edict of lavish praise.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥郝孝德、孫宣雅、時季康、竇建德、魏刀兒等，往往屯聚，大至十萬，小至數千，寇掠河北。

translations.literal: At the time the bandit chiefs Hao Xiaode, Sun Xuanya, Shi Jikang, Dou Jiande, Wei Dao'er, and others were often encamped — the largest numbering one hundred thousand, the smallest several thousand — raiding and plundering Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandit chiefs such as Hao Xiaode, Sun Xuanya, Shi Jikang, Dou Jiande, and Wei Dao'er were encamped here and there — some with one hundred thousand men, others with only a few thousand — raiding Hebei.

sentences.zh: 辯進兵擊之，所往皆捷，深為群賊所憚。

translations.literal: Bian advanced his army to attack them. Wherever he went he was victorious and was deeply feared by the bandit hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Bian marched against them and was victorious wherever he went, and the bandit hosts came to fear him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及翟讓寇徐、豫，辯進，頻擊走之。

translations.literal: When Zhai Rang raided Xu and Yu provinces, Bian advanced and repeatedly drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhai Rang raided Xu and Yu, Bian advanced and repeatedly drove him off.

sentences.zh: 讓尋與李密屯據洛口倉，辯與王世充討密，阻洛水相持經年。

translations.literal: Rang soon joined Li Mi in occupying Luokou Granary. Bian and Wang Shichong campaigned against Mi and faced each other across the Luo River for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Rang soon joined Li Mi in holding Luokou Granary. Bian and Wang Shichong campaigned against Mi and faced each other across the Luo River for a full year.

sentences.zh: 辯率諸將攻敗密，因薄其營，戰破外柵。

translations.literal: Bian led the generals in defeating Mi, pressed close to his camp, and in battle broke through the outer palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Bian led the generals in defeating Mi, pressed close to his camp, and broke through the outer stockade.

sentences.zh: 密諸營已有潰者，乘勝將入城，世充不知，恐將士勞倦，於是鳴角收兵，翻為密徒所乘。

translations.literal: Several of Mi's camps had already broken. Seizing victory, [Bian] was about to enter the city. Shichong did not know this and, fearing his officers and soldiers were weary, sounded the horn to recall the troops — and in the reversal Mi's followers seized the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Several of Mi's camps had already broken, and Bian was pressing the victory toward the city. Shichong did not know this and, fearing his men were exhausted, sounded the horn to recall the army — and Mi's followers turned the moment against them.

sentences.zh: 官軍大潰，不可救止。

translations.literal: The government army suffered a great rout that could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The government army collapsed in a rout that could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 辯至洛水，橋已壞，不得渡，遂涉水，至中流，為溺人所引墜馬。

translations.literal: Bian reached the Luo River. The bridge was already destroyed and he could not cross. He waded into the river, and at midstream drowning men pulled him off his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Bian reached the Luo River, but the bridge was already destroyed and he could not cross. He waded in, and at midstream drowning men pulled him off his horse.

sentences.zh: 辯時身被重甲，敗兵前後相蹈藉，不能復上馬，竟溺死焉。

translations.literal: Bian was then wearing heavy armor. The routed soldiers trampled one another before and behind him. He could not mount again and ultimately drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was wearing heavy armor. Routed soldiers trampled one another before and behind him, he could not mount again, and in the end he drowned.

sentences.zh: 時年五十六。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 三軍莫不痛惜之。

translations.literal: The whole army mourned him with deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 斛斯萬善河南斛斯萬善，驍勇果毅，與辯齊名。

translations.literal: Husi Wanshan—Husi Wanshan of Henan was bold, brave, and resolute, famed alongside Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Wanshan of Henan was bold, brave, and resolute, and was as famous as Bian.

sentences.zh: 大業中，從衛玄討楊玄感，頻戰有功。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he followed Wei Xuan in campaigning against Yang Xuangan and repeatedly distinguished himself in battle.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he followed Wei Xuan against Yang Xuangan and repeatedly distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗走，萬善與數騎追及之，玄感窘迫自殺。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was defeated and fled, Wanshan with several horsemen overtook him. Xuangan, in desperate straits, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was defeated and fled, Wanshan overtook him with a few horsemen. Xuangan, cornered, killed himself.

sentences.zh: 由是知名，拜武賁郎將。

translations.literal: Because of this he became renowned and was appointed Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he became famous and was made Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 突厥始畢之圍雁門也，萬善奮擊之，所向皆破。

translations.literal: When Shibi Khan of the Turks besieged Yanmen, Wanshan fought fiercely. Wherever he went he broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shibi Khan of the Turks besieged Yanmen, Wanshan fought fiercely and broke the enemy wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 每賊至，輒出當其鋒，或下馬坐地，引強弓射賊，所中皆殪。

translations.literal: Whenever bandits arrived he would go out to meet their vanguard. Sometimes he dismounted and sat on the ground, drew a powerful bow, and shot the bandits — every shot killed its target.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the enemy came he went out to meet their vanguard. Sometimes he dismounted, sat on the ground, and shot them with a powerful bow — every arrow found its mark.

sentences.zh: 由是突厥莫敢逼城，十許日竟退，萬善之力也。

translations.literal: Because of this the Turks did not dare press the city. After some ten days they finally withdrew — this was Wanshan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the Turks did not dare press the city. After some ten days they withdrew at last — and that was Wanshan's doing.

sentences.zh: 其後頻討群盜，累功至將軍。

translations.literal: Afterward he repeatedly campaigned against bandit hosts and accumulated merit until he reached the rank of general.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he repeatedly campaigned against bandits and rose through merit to the rank of general.

sentences.zh: 時有將軍鹿願、范貴、馮孝慈，俱為將帥，數從征討，並有名於世。

translations.literal: At the time Generals Lu Yuan, Fan Gui, and Feng Xiaoci were all commanders who repeatedly joined campaigns and were all famed in their time.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Generals Lu Yuan, Fan Gui, and Feng Xiaoci were all commanders who repeatedly joined campaigns and were all famous in their day.

sentences.zh: 然事皆亡失，故史官無所述焉。

translations.literal: But their deeds have all been lost, so the historiographers have nothing to record about them.
translations.idiomatic: But their deeds have all been lost, so the historiographers have nothing to say about them.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：楚、漢未分，絳、灌所以宣力；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Before Chu and Han were divided, it was for this that the Marquis of Jiang and Guan Ying were able to deploy their strength;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Before Chu and Han had been divided, men like the Marquis of Jiang and Guan Ying found occasion to prove their worth;

sentences.zh: 曹、劉競逐，關、張所以立名。

translations.literal: When Cao and Liu vied in pursuit, it was for this that Guan Yu and Zhang Fei were able to establish their names.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao and Liu contended for supremacy, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei found occasion to make their names.

sentences.zh: 然則名立資草昧之初，力宣候經輪之會，攀附鱗翼，世有之矣。

translations.literal: Thus reputation is established by drawing on the age when order was still in the rough; strength is deployed awaiting the moment when grand designs are set in motion. Clinging to dragon scales and phoenix wings — the world has always had such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Thus fame is won by those who rise in the earliest days of a new order, and strength is proved by those who wait for the moment when great plans are being laid. Riding the coattails of dragon and phoenix — the world has always known such men.

sentences.zh: 圓通、護兒之輩，定和、鐵杖之倫，皆一時之壯士，困于貧賤。

translations.literal: Men like Yuantong and Hu'er, and the likes of Dinghe and Tiezhang — all were warriors of their age, trapped in poverty and low station.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yuantong and Hu'er, and warriors like Dinghe and Tiezhang, were all bold men of their time, yet trapped in poverty and low station.

sentences.zh: 當其鬱抑未遇，亦安知其有鴻鵠之志哉！

translations.literal: When they were suppressed and had not yet met opportunity, who could have known they harbored the ambition of a great swan!
translations.idiomatic: When they were still obscure and had not yet found their moment, who could have guessed they harbored the ambition of a soaring swan!

sentences.zh: 終能振拔污泥之中，騰躍風雲之上，符馬革之願，快生平之心，非遇其時，焉能至於此也！

translations.literal: In the end they were able to pull themselves up from the mud, leap above the storm clouds, fulfill the vow to die with one's horse hide, and satisfy their hearts in life — had they not met their moment, how could they have reached this!
translations.idiomatic: In the end they pulled themselves up from the mud, leapt above the storm clouds, fulfilled the soldier's vow to die on campaign, and satisfied their hearts in life — had they not met their moment, how could they have reached such heights!

sentences.zh: 俱羅欲加之罪，非其咎畔，王辯殞身勍敵，志實勤王。

translations.literal: When Juluo was to have guilt attached to him, it was not for his fault of rebellion. Wang Bian perished before a fierce foe; his purpose was truly to serve the dynasty loyally.
translations.idiomatic: When guilt was to be attached to Juluo, it was not for any fault of rebellion on his part. Wang Bian died before a fierce foe, yet his purpose was truly to serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 陳棱縞素發喪，哀感行路，義之所動，固已深乎！

translations.literal: Chen Leng donned white hemp and held funeral rites. His grief moved passersby on the road. What righteousness can move — surely runs deep indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Leng donned white mourning dress and held funeral rites for the Emperor. His grief moved everyone on the road. When righteousness moves a man, it runs deep indeed!

sentences.zh: 孟才、錢傑、沈光等，感恩懷舊，臨難忘生，雖功無所成，其志有可稱矣。

translations.literal: Mengcai, Qian Jie, Shen Guang, and others, grateful and remembering old ties, faced danger without clinging to life. Though their achievements came to nothing, their purpose deserves praise.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai, Qian Jie, Shen Guang, and others, grateful and faithful to old ties, faced danger without clinging to their lives. Though their deeds came to nothing, their purpose deserves praise.
